title: Ukrainian authorities report hundreds of graves at a burial site near Izium
body:
In mid-September 2022, days after Ukrainian forces retook Izium on 10 September, investigators began excavating a burial site in a pine forest near the city in Kharkiv Oblast. Izium had been under Russian occupation for about five months. CNN reported on 16 September 2022 that Ukraine's Defense Ministry said at least 440 unmarked graves had been found.

Kharkiv Governor Oleh Syniehubov put the number of civilian bodies buried in the forest at 450 and said that 99 percent of the exhumed bodies showed signs of violent death. Some had their hands tied behind their back and one had a rope around its neck. Children were among the dead. President Volodymyr Zelensky said some bodies showed signs of torture and blamed Russia, calling the events cruelty and terrorism. Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications said the corpses were mostly civilians, and Human Rights Commissioner Dmytro Lubinets also described burials of servicemen, some with hands tied.

CNN reported that a UN human rights monitoring team was expected to visit Izium as soon as possible and that a war crimes investigation team might follow. Missing persons commissioner Oleh Kotenko warned that parts of the area remained mined. The report did not include a statement from Russian authorities.
